request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Admission date: N/A
Discharge date: N/A

Patient Information: 
The patient is a 71-year-old Finnish male diagnosed with early onset Parkinson's disease at the age of 40.

Hospital Course:

During the years 2016-2017, the patient was categorized at stage 2.5 of the modified Hoehn and Yahr Scale, with a United Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale (UPDRS) score of 41/199. The patient demonstrated rigidity of the lower limbs, shortness of steps, and postural instability, but no tremors. He has experienced a mild gait disturbance with occasional freezing recently. The progression of his illness has been slow, with a sustained response to medication.

Diagnostic Tests:
Dopamine transporter (DaT) single-photon emission computerized tomography (SPECT) of the brain was performed and demonstrated reduced density of DA synaptic terminals in the caudate and putamen consistent with degenerative Parkinson's disease.

Medical History:
The patient has no reported family history of Parkinson's disease.

Genetic Analysis:
Targeted next-generation sequencing revealed that the patient carried a novel homozygous c.194G > A variant in exon 3 of the PARK2 gene, causing an amino acid change p.Ser65Asn (S65N) in the PARKIN protein. The variant is very rare, but the site is highly conserved in vertebrates, and in silico analysis of the variant predicted that the mutation is deleterious.
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Follow-Up Care and Recommendations:
The patient should follow up with his healthcare provider regularly to monitor his condition and adjust medication as needed. The patient should be advised to continue engaging in regular physical activity and cognitive stimulation.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
CODE: G20

This is Parkinson disease (G20). The episode centres on the established diagnosis of degenerative Parkinson disease, confirmed by DaT SPECT and supported by the clinical picture. The PARK2 variant describes the genetic basis of the disease rather than a separate condition, so it does not change the category.
